questions.question:
Which query of the Person and Employment tables ONLY gets a person’s name and job
title, for all people that have jobs?

Look at the following query of the Person and Employment tables:

SELECT *
FROM Person AS p
LEFT JOIN Employment AS e ON p.Id = e.EmployeeId
WHERE e.Id IS NULL;

Which of the following best describes the query’s behavior?
options: Selects all people who are unemployed
Selects all people who are employed
Selects all Employment records that match to a Person record

questions.question:
In relational databases, entity integrity is the practice of ensuring each row in a table
_____?
options: Is different from all the other records

questions.question: What property does a primary key not need to maintain entity integrity?
options: All properties are required to maintain entity integrity

questions.question: Stored procedures can help prevent SQL injection by ______.
options: Allowing the execution of custom SQL from the user
Allowing the user to define parameters for the stored procedure
Only allowing user input through predefined parameters

Would it be more or less efficient to make the query a stored procedure?
options: More efficient, storing the query in physical memory takes too much space
More efficient, reading the query from memory will take less time
Less efficient, reading the query from memory will take more time

TO DISK = ‘D:/Backup’
WITH DIFFERENTIAL;

Creates a full backup of the production database to ‘D:/Backup’
